# PayFlow Data Platform

End-to-end data engineering platform for a fictional digital-payments fintech.
Synthetic data, 100% open-source stack, two parallel pipelines (batch + streaming).

## Purpose

Portfolio project demonstrating production data engineering patterns:
medallion lakehouse, real-time fraud scoring, ML feedback loop, pipeline orchestration.

## Stack

- Simulation: Python, Faker, NumPy (simulator/)
- Sources: PostgreSQL 16 (pgvector), MongoDB 7, FastAPI FX rates API
- Ingestion: Airbyte (Postgres incremental via xmin, MongoDB full-refresh)
- Lakehouse: Cloudflare R2 (Parquet + Delta Lake)
- Transform: dbt + DuckDB (httpfs reads Parquet directly from R2)
- Orchestration: Prefect 3 (hourly batch pipeline)
- ML: XGBoost + scikit-learn + MLflow (SQLite tracking)
- Streaming: Apache Kafka + kafka-python consumer
- Merchant normalization: pgvector + sentence-transformers embeddings
- Warehouse: BigQuery (payflow_analytics dataset)
- BI: Looker Studio
- Observability: Prefect UI (batch pipeline) + Grafana/Prometheus (real-time streaming)
- CI: GitHub Actions (dbt parse on every push, dbt test on main)

## Repository layout

simulator/           Synthetic transaction + fraud event generator (bulk_seed.py for bootstrap)
sources/postgres/    PostgreSQL schema: accounts, transactions, fraud_labels, fraud_scores
sources/fx-api/      FX rates microservice (FastAPI, port 8001)
ingestion/fx-connector/  Custom Airbyte CDK connector for the FX API
transform/           dbt project (payflow/): staging → silver → gold → marts
  models/staging/    Raw Bronze reads via DuckDB httpfs
  models/silver/     Typed, deduplicated, FX-normalized, PII-hashed (incremental)
  models/gold/       ML features + aggregates (full rebuild each run)
  models/marts/      BI-ready aggregates for Looker Studio
  seeds/             mcc_catalog.csv (981 MCC codes with risk_tier)
  tests/             Singular tests: fraud_rate bounds, amount_usd coverage
orchestration/       Prefect flows: normalize_merchants → dbt → BigQuery
ml/                  XGBoost training (train.py), FastAPI scoring service (serve.py)
  mlruns.db          MLflow SQLite tracking store
streaming/           Kafka producer (simulator) + fraud consumer (writes to Postgres)
infra/               Prometheus scrape config + Grafana dashboards (streaming observability)
scripts/             Utilities: abort_multipart.py, generate_mcc_catalog.py
docs/screenshots/    Evidence screenshots

## Key design decisions

- PII hashed before the lakehouse: email and holder_name are SHA-256 hashed in
  silver_accounts; raw values stay in PostgreSQL only. Salt omitted as portfolio
  simplification but the architectural boundary is correct.
- fraud_labels is a separate table: ground truth arrives days later via chargebacks,
  not at payment time. Embedding it in transactions creates ML leakage.
- silver_transactions is incremental (delete+insert); Gold is full rebuild each run.
- DuckDB reads Parquet from R2 via httpfs, no data movement, no cluster needed.
- pgvector normalizes merchant names before Gold is loaded to BigQuery.
- merchant excluded from ML features; mcc_category included instead; dirty name
  variants at training time would not generalize to unseen variants at inference.
- Fraud scoring thresholds: approve < 0.30, review 0.30–0.69, decline >= 0.70.
  FRAUD_THRESHOLD (0.50) is independent and used only for the is_fraud boolean.
- BigQuery Sandbox (free tier) expires 60 days after dataset creation.
  Re-run: python transform/load_to_bigquery.py

## CI

GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml):
- dbt-parse: runs on every push/PR, placeholder R2 credentials, validates SQL/YAML
- dbt-test: runs on main only, uses real R2 secrets, runs seed + run + test
